newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to issue T$3 billion in NCDs on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to issue T$3 billion in NCDs on Wednesday.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank said on Wednesday it would issue T$3 billion in seven-day negotiable certificates of deposit later in the day.
Bids would close at 11.15 local time (0315 GMT), a central bank official said.
The central bank gave no indication that it would expand the issue later in the day, as it did for the first time on Friday in a bid to check a stubborn rise in short-term interest rates.
The new issue is seen as compensating for the maturation on Wednesday of T$3 billion in NCDs, dealers said.
Taiwan's money rates closed higher on Tuesday amid tightening liquidity due to a booming stock market and depreciating Taiwan dollar.

Dealers said big turnover in the bourse was intensifying fund flows from the banking system, while the Taiwan dollar's tumble below T$28 to the U.S. dollar sparked concerns the central bank may intervene to support the currency. The rate finished at T$28.17, its lowest in more than eight years.
